adoption.notes: The runtime signs the unchanged command bytes and never reissues a command: egress publishes once, held by tests on its call sites, its scheduling and its client. It reads rate_limited only as a firmware-telemetry/v2 fault. It drives no firmware-commanded zone, so the Tier D attempt carve-out has no runtime path yet. No conformance claim is made, so the version is not frozen by this merge. It publishes liveness at v 1 only: it generates no nonce and keeps no liveness table. It signs commands and liveness over the object bytes alone, not yet in the domains of Signing Domains.

Its device verifier implements runtime liveness at v 1, which firmware-commands/v1's baseline audit moved to this version's Runtime Liveness section, and records whether the runtime is reachable as shadow observability. It signs the rate_limited verdict at fault v 2 from a3c54c2, and does not yet accept liveness at v 2. No conformance claim is made. Its verifiers check commands and liveness over the object bytes alone, not yet in the domains of Signing Domains.

notes: Exists for the rate_limited verdict, which answers relay_close only, and for the rule that a runtime never reissues a command to recover its delivery. Fresh open_protected_circuit attempts for a latched Tier D trip are not reissues and continue, under the binding the governing safety-profile contract authorizes. Command and provisioning approval bytes are v1's and keep v 1. Runtime liveness at v 1 keeps the grammar of this version's Runtime Liveness section and gains v 2, carrying a fresh 128-bit nonce from which the signing runtime bounds how long ago a device began the transaction behind a reading, under firmware-telemetry/v2; nothing implements liveness v 2 yet. Runtime liveness at v 1 is implemented by the runtime signer and the edge firmware verifier, which is implementation and not end-to-end or HIL proof; no device image gates a Local Interlock on it. The runtime has adopted the rate_limited and no-reissue rules; the edge firmware signs the rate_limited verdict from a3c54c2. The runtime adopts it before any device signs a v 2 fault, and devices accept liveness v 2 before the runtime publishes it. The runtime command key signs a command and a liveness message only in the domain of its purpose, under Signing Domains, and keeps no v 1 form; neither implementation signs or verifies in those domains yet, and the two switch together, since a runtime and a device on different sides of the switch refuse each other's commands and liveness.
